correctness.rationale: Direct four-case proof covers all n,k>=1. The first degree partition for n<=k+4 has t<=3 two-element cells and a universal core; all matching blocks form a forest so a coupled graph is determined by the stable equitable quotient. For k=1 path peeling recovers the reflection pair layers. For k>=2 and n>=k+5, three stable pair cells support a two-edge switch, preserving every refinement colour while destroying the two three-colour triangles. The explicit scripts verify the critical boundary arithmetic and switching for 2016 and 1258 finite parameter tests respectively; the proof, not these tests, covers the infinite range.

value.rationale: Path powers are a natural two-parameter family of proper interval graphs. The uniform sharp phase transition establishes exactly which are uniquely determined by low-variable counting logic among arbitrary graphs; both the constructive positive range and the two-edge negative witness are informative. This is an all-size structural classification, not a modest census or normalization exercise.
